text:
Devon: heads up — nightly perf alerted a regression on prefill-heavy workloads. p99 latency up ~18% for seqlen 32-128 vs last week. dashboard: https://dash.internal/r/bench/seqlen-prefill (see job 2026-03-16)
Devon: repro run attached below, reproduces locally on a40 pool:
```bash
./bench_runner --model redwood-ml/small --mode prefill --seq-len 64 --batch 8 --iters 500 --profile=nvprof
```
Anya: can you paste the exact perf numbers? quick summary is fine.
Devon: sure — raw numbers from the run (median over 5 runs):
- seq=32 batch=16 prefill path: p50=12ms, p95=48ms, p99=82ms
- seq=64 batch=8 prefill path: p50=20ms, p95=76ms, p99=110ms
- baseline (last good): p99 for seq64 was ~93ms
Mike: I looked at the nvprof traces — kernel selection switched from our fused-attn-cu to cuBLAS-gemm for the prefill matmul on that commit. flamegraph: https://flame.internal/1234
Mike: snippet from the kernel logger:
```
[autotune] selected algo cuBLAS_gemm_ex for QK matmul (shape 64x64x4096) on sm80
previously picked: fused_attn_fb (custom kernel)
reason: autotune score +3.2 for throughput metric
```
Ria: that explains it. fused_attn has higher latency per-op for short seqlen but better end-to-end critical path because it avoids extra memcopies and KV reformatting. cuBLAS wins raw GFLOPS but adds layout conversions -> hurts small seq.
OliveR: @Ria *agree* — prefill path is sensitive because we write KV in a dense layout for decoding. If kernel changes add an extra transpose, KV cache write time increases.
Anya: do we have per-stage breakdown? prefill decode vs kv write vs kernel exec?
Devon: yes, profiler breakdown from the failing run:
- total prefill step: 110ms
  - tokenization & inputs: 4ms
  - matmul (QK + attn): 54ms
  - KV pack/write: 28ms
  - misc (memcpy + cuda streams): 24ms
Devon: previous good run (same batch/seq) had matmul 46ms, KV pack 21ms, misc 22ms -> overall 92ms
Mike: autotune ranking currently uses a single composite score weighted to throughput. That makes it pick cuBLAS for shapes with high ops even if latency-critical paths cost more due to mem overhead.
Ria: proposal: make architecture-aware penalties for layout conversion and KV write impact. In autotune scoring add a penalty term: penalty = alpha * layout_convert_cost + beta * kv_write_delta (measured)
Ria: example config (RFC-ish):
```yaml
autotune:
  weights:
    throughput: 0.6
    latency_critical: 0.4
  penalties:
    layout_conversion_alpha: 1.5
    kv_write_beta: 2.0
  bucket_rules:
    - max_seq: 128
      prefer: fused_attn
    - min_seq: 129
      prefer: cuBLAS
```
Oliver: I ran a quick patch locally that forces fused_attn for seq<=128 on sm80. Result for seq64: p99 down to 96ms (vs 110), p95 70ms. Seq512 unaffected.
Oliver: numbers:
- patched: seq64 p99=96ms p95=70ms
- master: seq64 p99=110ms p95=76ms
Devon: nice. Any KB implications for KV cache? Did you validate no regression for decode path?
Oliver: decode path unaffected — we only switched prefill kernel. KV write time dropped from 28ms to 22ms in the patch (so packed layout reduced). decode path stays with incremental KV append so no change.
Anya: can we add an integration test that asserts autotune chooses fused_attn for seq<=128 on sm80? maybe a small threshold-based unit test in autotune harness.
Mike: yes, add a test that runs autotune scoring simulation on sampled shapes and asserts ranking. We should also log the selected kernel and the score decomposition so future regressions are easier to triage.
Perf-bot: nightly-bench: 2026-03-16T03:12Z — job seqlen-suite: p99 delta +18% (trigger: kernel-selection-change commit abc123). See linked job: https://ci.internal/bench/abc123
Devon: next steps:
- Mike to prototype scoring change (add penalty terms) — PR
- Oliver to run broader matrix (sm75, sm80, sm90) across seq buckets and post numbers
- Anya to add autotune unit test + log decomposed scores
- Ria to draft RFC for bucket rules + default thresholds
Devon: I'll canary rollback the kernel pick for prefill on the hosted pool tonight if we don't have a PR in time. schedule quick sync in #eng-runtime at 10:30 PT?
Anya: ack. I'll start the test and add a failing test that captures current regression so CI prevents future regresses.
Mike: will push a draft PR tomorrow with perf harness artifacts attached.
Ria: thanks all — this pattern (cuBLAS wins on ops but loses on end-to-end latency) is recurring — we should capture it in autotune telemetry so the tuner learns over time.
Devon: thanks — logging action items into the incident board. :white_check_mark:
